units.text: INT. SEAGULL - CONTINUOUS
I am irresistibly impelled toward her. It may be that this is just what I need.
units.name: TRIGORIN

units.text: What, the love of a country girl? Oh, how little you know yourself!
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: People sometimes walk in their sleep, and so I feel as if I were asleep, and dreaming of her as I stand here talking to you. My imagination is shaken by the sweetest and most glorious visions. Release me!
units.name: TRIGORIN

units.text: Shuddering.
No, no! I am only an ordinary woman; you must not say such things to me. Do not torment me, Boris; you frighten me.
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: You could be an extraordinary woman if you only would. Love alone can bring happiness on earth, love the enchanting, the poetical love of youth, that sweeps away the sorrows of the world. I had no time for it when I was young and struggling with want and laying siege to the literary fortress, but now at last this love has come to me. I see it beckoning; why should I fly?
units.name: TRIGORIN

units.text: With anger.
You are mad!
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: Release me.
units.name: TRIGORIN

units.text: You have all conspired together to torture me to-day.
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: She weeps.
Clutching his head desperately.
She doesn’t understand me! She won’t understand me!
units.name: TRIGORIN

units.text: Am I then so old and ugly already that you can talk to me like this without any shame about another woman?
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: She embraces and kisses him.
Oh, you have lost your senses! My splendid, my glorious friend, my love for you is the last chapter of my life.
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: She falls on her knees.
You are my pride, my joy, my light.
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: She embraces his knees.
I could never endure it should you desert me, if only for an hour; I should go mad. Oh, my wonder, my marvel, my king!
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: Some one might come in.
units.name: TRIGORIN

units.text: He helps her to rise.
Let them come! I am not ashamed of my love.
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: She kisses his hands.
My jewel! My despair! You want to do a foolish thing, but I don’t want you to do it. I shan’t let you do it!
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: She laughs.

You are mine, you are mine! This forehead is mine, these eyes are mine, this silky hair is mine. All your being is mine. You are so clever, so wise, the first of all living writers; you are the only hope of your country. You are so fresh, so simple, so deeply humourous. You can bring out every feature of a man or of a landscape in a single line, and your characters live and breathe. Do you think that these words are but the incense of flattery? Do you think I am not speaking the truth? Come, look into my eyes; look deep; do you find lies there? No, you see that I alone know how to treasure you. I alone tell you the truth. Oh, my very dear, you will go with me? You will? You will not forsake me?
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: I have no will of my own; I never had. I am too indolent, too submissive, too phlegmatic, to have any. Is it possible that women like that? Take me. Take me away with you, but do not let me stir a step from your side.
units.name: TRIGORIN

units.text: To herself.
Now he is mine!
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: Carelessly, as if nothing unusual had happened.
Of course you must stay here if you really want to. I shall go, and you can follow in a week’s time. Yes, really, why should you hurry away?
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: Let us go together.
units.name: TRIGORIN

units.text: As you like. Let us go together then.
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: A pause.
TRIGORIN writes something in his note-book.
What are you writing?
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: A happy expression I heard this morning: “A grove of maiden pines.” It may be useful.
units.name: TRIGORIN

units.text: He yawns.
So we are really off again, condemned once more to railway carriages, to stations and restaurants, to Hamburger steaks and endless arguments!
units.name: TRIGORIN

units.text: SHAMRAEFF comes in.

I am sorry to have to inform you that your carriage is at the door. It is time to start, honoured madam, the train leaves at two-five. Would you be kind enough, madam, to remember to inquire for me where Suzdaltzeff the actor is now? Is he still alive, I wonder? Is he well? He and I have had many a jolly time together. He was inimitable in “The Stolen Mail.” A tragedian called Izmailoff was in the same company, I remember, who was also quite remarkable. Don’t hurry, madam, you still have five minutes. They were both of them conspirators once, in the same melodrama, and one night when in the course of the play they were suddenly discovered, instead of saying “We have been trapped!” Izmailoff cried out: “We have been rapped!”
units.name: SHAMRAEFF

units.text: He laughs.
Rapped!
units.name: SHAMRAEFF

units.text: While he has been talking JACOB has been busy with the trunks, and the maid has brought ARKADINA her hat, coat, parasol, and gloves.
The cook looks hesitatingly through the door on the right, and finally comes into the room.
PAULINA comes in.
MEDVIEDENKO comes in.
Presenting ARKADINA with a little basket.
